name: Marshal of the March
summary: Commands nothing that can be counted. The Marshal may close the river crossings and call the levy, and the levy is answered by people who may say no; what the Marshal has is authority over passage, never authority over a body.

provenance.author: tools lore ingest
basis: authored-game-data

attributes.material_cause: geography.widow_run relocates its bed far enough between floods to move every settlement on it, and cosmology.mortal_law_availability leaves spatial law unspent so no two surveys of the same ground agree. A polity that cannot measure itself can still count the one thing every body must do, which is cross water.
attributes.form_of_government: A ferry-polity, not a land state. Its five seats are filled from sects that were never related to one another (iron_vine, jade_court) and its land is a claim over places anyone holding the standing to contest them may contest. Government follows the river, which means it governs the crossing and never the ground.
attributes.law: Custom, and necessarily so: geography.hollow_measure makes every distance here unenforceable, so possession is proven by a marker standing and never by measuring where it stands. A land court on this tier could not enforce a judgement, so no institution here may levy a seat and no office may be sold.
attributes.economy: Paid in grain. The obligation line is two ford dues and one winter grain, which is the only denomination in which the payer and the payee both survive a bad year - and a tariff denominated in the payer's own crop cannot be inflated by anyone, because the collector eats from the same field.
attributes.infrastructure: Fords, bridges, a granary and a line of river lanterns. Every one of them is built to be rebuilt at the next flood, and the lanterns are currently unlit because the seat that lights them is vacant.
attributes.trade_network: The Tier Stair foot and the Cairn Field gate. There is no export: the tier's only marketable output is the crowd that comes to watch nine trials it is not licensed to attempt, so the March's trade is passage in and gate fees out.
attributes.why_this_form: Because the marsh's answer to iron exhaustion was not to find more iron but to move people off the ground that had none, and a polity that sells passage is the only kind that can survive its own country's depletion.
attributes.searched_for: lore search marshal / ford / river / polity returned only this record; no rival river polity exists.

name: Star Regent
summary: Sits where the crown is claimed to sit, which is a claim and not a crown. The Regent may name a seat and may not take one: every appointment goes through a trial the Regent cannot judge, which is what stops the highest office from being self-perpetuating.

provenance.author: tools lore ingest
basis: authored-game-data

attributes.material_cause: It sits on the first surveyed ground in the setting. geography.spirit_peaks writes spatial and temporal law, so a boundary there can be walked, measured and defended as a line - the first place in the setting where a claim becomes a border, and the only place a court can cite ground.
attributes.form_of_government: A precedent polity with four seats, and one of them has never been filled. The highest seat is filled by a three-stage trial the office cannot judge; the Reader grants access and no power; the Marshal of the Court is a pair, so neither can refuse the other's order alone and only the pair can seal an office; the Hermit of the Outer Seat is empty by design and always will be.
attributes.law: Precedent. The Reader of the Law sets which doctrine tier a case may be heard under, which is access and never power: it opens a shelf and grants nothing on the far side of it. A highland polity on surveyed ground can cite, and a precedent nobody may cite is not a rule but a private opinion.
attributes.economy: Standing 95 against an authored ceiling of 150, and an obligation worth exactly one term: court_etiquette. Its political range is the longest in the setting and the least legible, because fifty of its hundred-and-fifty possible points project no recognition at all - a third of the crown's politics exists in a currency nothing can read.
attributes.infrastructure: Terraces, precedent shelves and a court, all on highland, because the only ground worth citing is ground that can be measured. It also holds the immortal district above, which it governs from below its own Dao's home tier.
attributes.trade_network: The Gale Pass window and the shelf confederacy's harbours. Everything the Court buys arrives through a crossing somebody else schedules, which is the structural reason a highland court with a crown claim has never had a supply policy.
attributes.why_this_form: Because it is the only polity on ground where a border is a line, and because four vacant immortal seats were very nearly filled by decree once. The Vacancy Decree is not a limitation this court chose; it is the scar left by an attempt to govern the top tier by appointment.
attributes.searched_for: lore search star_regent / crown / court / highland returned only this record; no rival highland court exists.

name: The Ford Assembly
summary: The two banks of one ford, meeting at the crossing rather than beside it. It exists because distance is not conserved on the Mortal Plains, so the only boundary fact anybody can prove is that you may stand on one side and then the other inside a single hour - and this is the one place on the tier where that proof is available.

provenance.author: w3-civs
basis: authored-game-data:game/data/nation/march_of_the_nine_provinces.tres
abstract-pattern:ferry-company republics on tidal crossings
lore search ford / ford_assembly returned no prior record

attributes.material_cause: geography.widow_run moves its bed far enough between floods to relocate every settlement on it, so the ford is re-found every season rather than owned. Its meeting place is therefore a riverbed, and its charter is cut into a marker that a flood can read but not move.
attributes.form_of_government: Ferry-houses send delegates, and a ferry-house is a household that owns a boat - which on a river that relocates is the only form of capital worth defending. Delegations are seated in odd numbers as a standing rule, because two banks can deadlock and a deadlock on a ford is a flood with extra steps.
attributes.law: An agreement is witnessed or it is a rumour. The Assembly has no scribe to improve on the river culture's own rule and has never wanted one, because a written minute would outlast the crossing that produced it.
attributes.economy: Ferry dues in grain and salt, and salt is the unit because it is the one good the plains cannot grow while grain is the unit because it is the one good they cannot do without. Dues are re-fixed each flood and published at both landings the same day.
attributes.infrastructure: Two landing stages, one mooring rope and one bell. The rope is cut and re-tied every flood; the bell is rung once for a crossing and twice for a refusal, and the Assembly counts the second kind every year without publishing the total.
attributes.trade_network: The Widow Run south to the Tier Stair foot and north to the crossings the Charterhouse underwrites - two ends, one rope between them.
attributes.why_it_exists: Because the March needs a place where its highest oath is sworn. The office is a trial, its first stage is sworn at the ford, and a stage cannot be administered by the office it produces, so the swearing happens here and the naming happens somewhere else entirely.

name: Plainstoll
summary: The town at the foot of the Tier Stair, and the only settlement on the mortal tier whose entire population is visitors - including its own officers, because a world with three law seats licenses plants and beasts and admits no humanoid to be native. It exists because arrival is repeatable here and departure is not, so a stranger's first act is a transaction and their last is unrecorded.

provenance.author: w3-civs
basis: authored-game-data:geography.mortal_plains.faction_id=body_dao with available_life_forms plant+beast
abstract-pattern:caravan toll towns at a hard frontier
lore search stair / toll-town / plainstoll returned no prior record

attributes.material_cause: geography.tier_stair is the only graded route off the plains. Arrival is repeatable because the road measures itself and departure is not, because spatial law is unspent and the return walk's distance cannot be established - so every permanent resident here arrived, and not one of them can prove they will leave.
attributes.form_of_government: A chartered toll whose charter is the foot of the stair and nothing else. It is forfeit the moment the stair foot moves, which has happened twice, and both times the town was re-chartered by whoever held the field at the time rather than by anyone who had held it before.
attributes.law: Entry is licensed, never owned. The town's own instrument is a licensing table, and it says so: a traveller owes the marshal nothing and the house everything. There is no land deed on this tier because no deed could be enforced against an unmeasured distance.
attributes.economy: Gate fees from the Cairn Field crowd. It is the only tax the plains can actually collect, because the crowd is the only export a resource-poor tier has - and the local households pay it too, since they are spectators as well and are not exempt from their own town's gate.
attributes.infrastructure: A graded yard that measures itself, a stair-head hut, and a field of pale lichen patches recording where trials have been held. The yard is re-graded every flood season, which is the whole of its municipal works budget.
attributes.trade_network: The Tier Starr down to the Cairn Field, the Charterhouse road west, and the flats garrison east across the spoil. Three ends, and the town is the only thing all three agree to meet at.
attributes.why_it_exists: Because the stairs only door into the plains is also the only door out, so every practitioner who has ever attempted a mortal-band trial has walked through this yard - and the tier cannot produce one of them, which makes the town a customs house for a population it does not have.

name: Flatswatch
summary: A garrison holding ground its own faction cannot staff from. The Mortal Plains is Body Dao's home tier and licenses no humanoid, so every soul inside these walls is a visitor from a world with a larger law budget - and the walls are held by people whose trade, family and loyalty are all somewhere else. It exists because a faction that claims a tier it cannot reproduce in has exactly one option: send outsiders and rotate them.

provenance.author: w3-civs
basis: authored-game-data:geography.mortal_plains faction_id body_dao + cosmology.mortal_law_availability resident forms plant/beast
abstract-pattern:frontier garrisons held by a distant centre
lore search forward / garrison / flats / fort returned no prior record

attributes.material_cause: geography.mortal_plains carries faction_id body_dao and authored life forms of plant and beast only, and cosmology.body_dao records Body Dao's home_tier as mortal_world. The faction's home ground is therefore the one place its own practitioners cannot be born, and a home ground you cannot replenish is a garrison post.
attributes.form_of_government: Rotating garrison under a fixed-term charter with no renewal clause for the same detachment. The rotation is the constitution: it is the only defence the post has against a commander who has decided to stay, and it is also the reason no garrison here has ever had local knowledge of anything.
attributes.law: The garrison may hold the working face and may not settle anyone. Occupation is temporary by construction, because geography.ironhead_flats is only worth holding while the seam is being worked, and the moment it stops being worked the post is required to stand down whether or not the order arrives.
attributes.economy: Paid in gate-fee shares and iron allotments. It is the single largest standing buyer of iron_ore on the tier, which is precisely why it and the field households are permanent opponents over one seam - and its allotments are the reason the face is worked faster than the spoil can be cleared.
attributes.infrastructure: A working face, a spoil line, a barrack and a wall. The wall faces outward against nothing in particular, because the garrison's actual threat is its own term expiring rather than an army.
attributes.trade_network: The flats to the Tier Stair gate westward, and the seam to the plain households southward. The garrison is the second of the two ends of the only road that crosses the spoil.
attributes.why_it_exists: Because Body Dao is a territory-holding Dao and not an academy, and a Dao whose home tier licenses no humanoid must garrison that tier with people it raised somewhere else. The garrison is the price of calling a law-poor world a home.

name: The Spiritscar Company
summary: A chartered town at the mouth of the only verifiable hole in the setting. It exists because the quarry answers how much spirit stone the ridge has left per unit of ground worked, the answer has been falling for three generations, and only a measurement nobody can edit survives - which means the company's product is a falling number held in public.

provenance.author: w3-civs
basis: authored-game-data:geography.spiritscar_quarry + history.consequence_the_density_ceiling
abstract-pattern:assay and survey offices attached to mines
lore search quarry / assay / spiritscar / company returned no prior settlement

attributes.material_cause: geography.spiritscar_quarry is a hole you can stand in and see the end of, and verification there means digging. It is the only institution in the setting that measures a world rather than praising it, which makes it the only place where a claim about scarcity can be checked by anybody who cares to check.
attributes.form_of_government: A chartered company whose charter is renewed only while the measured figure keeps falling. Stagnation does not void it; silence does. A company that stopped publishing would still hold the charter, and this has been argued about in three consecutive years.
attributes.law: The face book is open and the assay floor is neutral ground. No buyer may dispute a figure that was published before the sale, which shifts every argument from after the fact to before it and is the only enforcement mechanism the company has.
attributes.economy: Paid in measurement fees and in assay time, and its customers are people deciding whether to cross the ridge at all - so its real revenue is the confidence of a market rather than the stone it cuts. Stone revenue exists and is not what keeps the charter alive.
attributes.infrastructure: A working face, an assay floor, a spoil cut that has not dispersed in decades, and a tide calendar that gates every trial booked on the adjoining Sixth Seat Grounds. The calendar is the most valuable structure on the site and it is a schedule, not a building.
attributes.trade_network: Galehold at the pass above, the Jade Holdfast beyond it, and Flame Valley at the far end of the same window. The Company sells access to a number and the number sells the road.
attributes.why_it_exists: Because somebody has to be right about the Density Ceiling in public. Every party that benefits from a falling answer has an interest in a hole nobody can look into, and an institution that publishes before it sells is the only counterweight the setting has produced.

name: Galehold
summary: The polity that holds the only crossing of the Sixfold Ridge, and whose calendar is not its own. The window is set by the Tidemark season and its worst hours are occupied by the swift flock, so the holder sets the price and never the date - the only arrangement in the setting that makes a toll defensible and a timetable not.

provenance.author: w3-civs
basis: authored-game-data:geography.sixfold_ridge + geography.gale_pass + ecology.gale_pass_swift
abstract-pattern:customs houses at an orographic pass
lore search gale / pass-state / galehold returned no prior polity

attributes.material_cause: geography.sixfold_ridge is one wall carrying spirit_stone and jade_ore in the same bedding, and geography.gale_pass is its single crossing. A claim on either deposit is therefore a claim on the other and on the pass, which is the setting's one clean instance of a resource creating a border.
attributes.form_of_government: A window-keeper's council, one seat per house that can afford to be wrong about the weather. The council cannot change the window, which means it can only distribute the consequences of one - and every member who over-reports a windfall is replaced, because a house that loses money on a bad window does not re-sit.
attributes.law: The window is published a season ahead and may not be shortened. Shortening it is the one act this polity cannot commit, because a shortened window converts a schedule into a claim on the weather, and weather is the one thing nobody here has ever successfully claimed.
attributes.economy: Toll on weight, never on value. A caravan carrying a thing whose price nobody will name pays the same as one carrying grain, which is the only reason this is the single road the Unfiled community can afford - and the reason the holder can never tell what is moving through.
attributes.infrastructure: One cut road, one cairn of published markers, and a wind-break. The markers are cut annually and the previous year's are left standing, so the road is also the only honest record of who crossed when.
attributes.trade_network: The Jade Holdfast and Flame Valley behind the pass, the Spiritscar Company and the Shelf League in front. Two ends and one schedule, and the holder's power is entirely in the schedule's being readable.
attributes.why_it_exists: Because one geological accident put two resources in one bedding behind one crossing. That is the whole cause: nothing here was founded for defence or for prestige, and the polity is legible entirely as the price of a chokepoint nobody could widen.

name: The Long Ration
summary: A holdfast on the far side of the Gale Pass where jade runs as a gradient rather than a pocket, so the people who cut it live in falling series of thin, hard, increasingly deep workings and cannot grow a crop on any of them. It exists because jade holds qi and will not give it up, which makes the cleft the spirit tier's best refinement ground and its worst farming ground - and so whoever feeds the cleft owns it more durably than whoever mines it.

provenance.author: w3-civs
basis: authored-game-data:geography.jade_cleft + ecology.jade_seam_draft + ecology.jade_cleft_moss
abstract-pattern:company towns holding non-farmable mineral ground
lore search jade / cleft / holdfast returned no prior settlement

attributes.material_cause: geography.jade_cleft will not grow a crop and is reachable only through geography.gale_pass, while ecology.jade_seam_draft makes the seam a gradient to be followed rather than a pocket to be emptied. The result is a settlement that cannot feed itself and cannot be reached by anyone who chooses not to carry for it.
attributes.form_of_government: A holdfast chartered by its ration rather than by its lease: the charter lapses when the food does, and the food arrives on a road somebody else schedules. Governance is therefore a queue for the next delivery, and the queue is the only office anybody wants.
attributes.law: The ration book is the constitution. Every dispute is settled by reading it aloud, because there is no second record and no scribe, and because a book that is read aloud in front of the hungry is harder to alter than a book that is not.
attributes.economy: Buys everything and sells jade. The exchange rate is set by the pass-holder rather than by the cleft, which is the entire reason the cleft has never once been independent, and it stays that way for as long as the food and the road arrive from the same direction.
attributes.infrastructure: Working faces strung down a gradient, a moss-cut boundary that dies back over every face cut, and a store that must be restocked before the window closes. The boundary is the only map of the seam and every day's work destroys a piece of it.
attributes.trade_network: Galehold at the pass, the Spiritscar Company at the near end of the same road, and no third direction at all. It is a settlement with one exit, which is why its food contract and its price agree.
attributes.why_it_exists: Because the cleft's product is the only material in the setting that will not release what it holds, which makes it valuable, and because the gradient cannot be worked without provisioning, which makes the provisioner the durable party. The mine was always going to belong to the road.

name: The Two Shores
summary: A league of the two coasts of the Cloudshelf Sea, formed the moment the sea became worth owning. It exists because this is the first tier where a coastline holds its shape and a kelp bed keeps to a written season, so a boat is an asset and a harvest can be contracted against - and because a league is the only form that lets both shores admit they need each other without either conceding the water.

provenance.author: w3-civs
basis: authored-game-data:geography.cloudshelf_sea + ecology.cloudshelf_kelp + ecology.cloudshelf_hunter + cosmology.spirit_law_availability
abstract-pattern:confederated coastal trading houses
lore search cloudshelf / league / two shores returned no prior polity

attributes.material_cause: geography.cloudshelf_sea holds its coastline because spatial law is written at this tier, and its kelp keeps to a cycle because temporal and elemental law are written too. Below this tier a border is a claim that can be argued; here it is water that drowns you, and it feeds on a schedule.
attributes.form_of_government: A league, not a state. No member owns a crossing, by written rule, because a crossing is a monopoly and a monopoly on water is a claim on the sea itself. The league therefore has no seat that any member can hold, which is the only reason both shores signed.
attributes.law: Two rules and no others: no member may own a crossing, and no member may name a price in open water. The second rule exists because a price stated once in the league's own channel is a price the kelp season cannot sustain, and every attempt to state one has become a war.
attributes.economy: Harvest contracts written against the Tidemark, salt out and kelp in, and a licensed predator to eat what is farmed. ecology.cloudshelf_hunter is licensed rather than tolerated, so the league farms the risk as well as the crop and sells the surplus of one shore to the shore that cannot fish this season.
attributes.infrastructure: Two harbours, one agreed boundary laid in stones and reset every season, and a kelp line that stops on the day the Tidemark turns against it. The boundary stones are the league's only physical asset and both shores move them together.
attributes.trade_network: Galehold at the single pass inland, the Brine Reach for salt, and the unlisted anchorage on the far water for anything either shore will not register. Three ends, and the third is the reason the league can negotiate at all.
attributes.why_it_exists: Because the first tier that can hold a coastline also makes a boat a durable asset, and two durable assets on opposite banks of one sea produce either a war or a league. The league exists because the alternative was a war over a fish nobody could farm alone.

name: The Unlisted Anchorage
summary: An anchorage added to the settlement the Void Serpent caravan collapse left, not a rival to it. It exists because a counting house publishes credit, safe-conduct and trading posts against exclusivity, and a community that will not accept exclusivity has to become impossible to enumerate - so the people who would not take the terms took the one berth no ledger admits to owning.

provenance.author: w3-civs
basis: authored-game-data:cultures.weight_and_name cause field + cultures.unfiled cause field + organizations.saltledger exclusivity
abstract-pattern:unregistered anchorage economies
lore search anchorage / unfiled / berth returned no prior settlement

attributes.material_cause: cultures.weight_and_name is the one surviving settlement of the people who carried Void Serpents out of the Spirit Peaks and abandoned the ledger when the serpents' own law values wrote a number that could not be recorded. This is the berth their weight-only traders added after the Saltledger began quoting a price for every mooring on that water.
attributes.form_of_government: None, deliberately. No roll, no office, no minute. It is administered by whoever is standing at the time, and the arrangement is understood by everyone present not to outlive the tide. Its nearest relation to a constitution is that the counting houses are themselves owned vessels, so the accounting can leave when the accounting becomes unsafe.
attributes.law: Nothing written is nothing owed. An obligation exists between people who are present and stops being enforceable the moment they are not, which means the anchorage has no writs, no debt and no way to be annexed - and also no way to settle a dispute it has chosen to stop caring about.
attributes.economy: Weights, never prices. The standing name covers every commercial arrangement the community has ever made, and a hull's design is the legal statement that nothing on board is registered anywhere - which every other port reads as a promise of its own honesty and which is the only credit the anchorage has ever had.
attributes.infrastructure: Two owned vessels that are also the counting houses, a landing that can be struck in a day, and no permanent structure of any kind. Everything here is portable because a fixed structure is a place a list can be written about.
attributes.trade_network: Both shores of the Cloudshelf Sea, and the outer water past the shelf edge where the reach of any ledger stops. Two ends and neither of them is a register.
attributes.why_it_exists: Because a house that answers a carriage trade with prices at its own rates cannot enumerate a trade whose good is unrecorded. The pressure produced the most careful paperless culture in the setting, and this is the berth that pressure left behind.

name: The Terrace Council
summary: The body that decides who may step onto nine engraved terraces, and that cannot be a candidate for any of them. It exists because the highest office may name a seat and may not take one, and because a vacancy at this tier is a physical absence visible from the district below - so somebody has to be the judge who is structurally unable to be judged.

provenance.author: w3-civs
basis: authored-game-data:history.decree_the_unfilled_seats + geography.terrace_of_nine_seats + game/data/nation/court_of_the_star.tres
abstract-pattern:collegiate courts with rotating parity rules
lore search conclave / terrace / seat council returned no prior polity

attributes.material_cause: history.decree_the_unfilled_seats exists because four vacant immortal seats were very nearly filled by decree, and that attempt is what taught this setting to write a vacancy as its own state. geography.terrace_of_nine_seats then made the vacancy physical - nine cut terraces shaped to forbid a second occupant, legible from the lower district.
attributes.form_of_government: Nine seats sat in odd numbers so a motion cannot tie. It can seat, unseat and refuse. It cannot dissolve a person, which is the only way this build dissolves anything, and it may not appoint itself - every candidate it hears has to be someone it has never sat beside.
attributes.law: Three states and no fourth: an empty record means the office does not exist; a vacancy means it exists and its value is absent; a refusal is a named reason. A vacancy is never a zero and never a hidden row, because hiding the row would say the office does not exist.
attributes.economy: It grants no stat at all. Recognition is projected as a bounded percent on an authored allowlist and never as a flat, never as a base write and never as a second composer - so the Council's entire economic product is access, and the standing that buys it is a different number from the standing it dispenses.
attributes.infrastructure: Nine terraces cut to one office each, a stair that can be closed, and a floor on which every past attempt is legible in rock. The rock is the reason the Council is trusted: a failed breakthrough scars the ground as well as the body, and the scar cannot be edited by whoever lost it.
attributes.trade_network: None. Its network is the court it sits over and the ring whose scarring schedule it times its sittings against.
attributes.why_it_exists: Because the Decree required an unjudgeable trial and a court with no unjudgeable trial is a court that cannot function. Nine seats and odd parity is the smallest body in this setting that can hear a case it is not party to and still produce a result nobody may appeal to itself.

name: The Brine Reach
summary: A dominion whose territory is exactly its waterline. It exists because the basin's brine is the one supply that never fails and everything else dies back, and because the specialised body that can drink it stops above the brine line - so the population of a salt dominion cannot be moved up the shore without ceasing to be the people it governs.

provenance.author: w3-civs
basis: authored-game-data:races.deepsalt + races.saltfolk + races.brinecaller
abstract-pattern:basin polities whose border is a waterline
lore search brine / salt-dominion / reach returned no prior polity

attributes.material_cause: races.deepsalt is a subspecies that exists because its parent body became a requirement rather than a habitat, and a brine line is therefore the dominion's border: nobody who is its subject can live above it. The Reach is not bounded by a treaty but by a species' metabolism, which is a border nobody can agree to move and nobody can survive moving past.
attributes.form_of_government: Hereditary brine-lodgings. A household's standing is the depth of water it may moor at, which is continuous, earned and can fall with the basin's own level - and which has nothing to do with which family holds which pier, because the two are settled by different procedures and read by different clerks.
attributes.law: Brine is apportioned, never sold. A family's allotment is a depth, and a depth rises and falls with the basin, so an allotment can shrink without anybody having done anything. This is the setting's one institution where the most important legal fact is a physical measurement, and it is the only place a standing can fall for no social reason at all.
attributes.economy: Salt is the currency because it is the only good that cannot be made here and can be carried by anything. Everything else is imported, which is why the Reach's leverage is not at its own shore but at the mouth of every import road, and why its quarrel with the counting houses is over harbour tariffs rather than over salt.
attributes.infrastructure: Evaporation terraces, mooring steps cut down the slope, and a brine line that must be re-surveyed every season because the level moves. The survey is the constitution's only amendment procedure and it is run by three lodgings that each get one clerk.
attributes.trade_network: Salt out to the Shelf League's shores, imports in through the harbours the counting houses rate, and a standing dispute with the Saltledger over which body sets the tariff. Three ends and only one of them is a person who can be argued with.
attributes.why_it_exists: Because the basin's supply is the one thing in the setting that never fails, and a community that can live where nothing else does acquires leverage without acquiring land - which is the whole reason its border is a depth of water and not a line on a map.

name: The Fresh-Break Claim
summary: A claim on ground whose value is already falling, held by people who cannot sell it and will not leave it. It exists because a dao fragment cures as it decays and a cured fragment is void crystal, so the shelf is the setting's only resource that is worthless before its owner is - which makes holding it without a buyer a liability and holding it with one a race.

provenance.author: w3-civs
basis: authored-game-data:geography.fragmentshelf + geography.void_expanse + geography.fragment_ring + cosmology.transcendent_law_availability
abstract-pattern:claims over a maturing mineral with a fixed conversion tail
lore search fragmentshelf / shelf claim / deadline territory returned no prior polity

attributes.material_cause: geography.fragmentshelf is workable only while the break is fresh and there is no way to slow curing, and the tier runs at ten to a hundred times a slower world's clock. A generation is therefore a working lifetime and a market lifetime at once, which is unique to this tier and is the whole of the claim's economics.
attributes.form_of_government: None that could be called a government. It is a queue for a window: the claim confers a right to cut, and the right expires whether or not anyone exercises it. Nobody administers the expiry, because an institution that administered it would be admitting that the resource is a fixed thing, and it is not.
attributes.law: Two incompatible rules in one place. geography.fragment_ring must stand on the shelf because broken law is the only substrate that can host a self larger than its container, so the trial ring and the mine compete for the same square - and the ring's scars cannot be edited by whoever lost them, which makes the only trustworthy record on this ground belong to the people who failed.
attributes.economy: Fragments are priced against the cure rather than against the buyer, and geography.void_expanse grows every period without being slowed, so the cured form is the one resource in the setting nobody can corner. What is worth holding is therefore the fresh end of a wound, and holding anything else is holding a liability with a maintenance bill.
attributes.infrastructure: A cut face, a trial ring, and a clock that is not a clock. The face cannot be planned further ahead than one cure cycle and cannot be abandoned without leaving the square to the ring, which is the trilemma this place is named for.
attributes.trade_network: Down the Third Layer Hold, which holds the surplus imprints rather than the goods, and out through the Rift Shore's door with a timetable. One way down and a door that closes on a cycle nobody sets.
attributes.why_it_exists: Because this is the only ground where the resource, the arena and the surplus sit on the same square. The claim is not a sovereignty; it is a queue, and the dispute recorded here is between the parties who need the same metres for incompatible reasons.
